title: shotgun-metagenomics-nf pipeline parameters
description: ONT shotgun metagenomics for Rapid Barcoding Kit (no PCR) reads: read QC, human read removal, taxonomic classification and AMR gene detection.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Samplesheet CSV with two columns: sample,fastq.
input.help_text: Each row maps a sample name to a fastq file or glob (e.g. `data/barcode17/*.fastq.gz`). A glob may match multiple part-files -- they're merged into one file per sample before filtering. Glob paths resolve relative to the launch directory, not the samplesheet's own location.

outdir.description: Output directory where results are published.

read_filtering.title: Read filtering
read_filtering.description: chopper length/quality filtering, before anything else.

min_len.help_text: Rapid-kit reads have no fixed length, so there's no maximum. Shorter reads are harder to classify reliably and can't cover a whole AMR gene.

min_qual.help_text: Q10 is about 1 error in 10 bases. R10.4.1 reads basecalled with dorado hac or sup are mostly well above this, so it mainly drops failed reads.

host_removal.title: Host read removal
host_removal.description: Deacon removes human reads before anything is published.

host_fasta.description: Host genome FASTA to build the removal index from, instead of the human pangenome.
host_fasta.help_text: Unset (the default), human reads are removed with Deacon's prebuilt panhuman-1 index. Set, an index is built from this FASTA instead, and human reads are then NOT removed unless it includes a human genome.

db_cache.description: Where downloaded databases are cached between runs.

taxonomic_classification.title: Taxonomic classification
taxonomic_classification.description: Kraken2 classifies each host-removed read against a prebuilt RefSeq database.

kraken2_db.description: Kraken2 database, downloaded once and cached.
kraken2_db.help_text: Both are the Langmead lab's June 2026 PlusPF build: RefSeq bacteria, archaea, viruses, plasmids, human, protozoa and fungi. pluspf16 (the default) is capped at 16 GB and needs about 20 GB of memory; pluspf8 is capped at 8 GB, needs about 10 GB, and misses more reads -- use it for testing or on a smaller machine, not for results you'll report.

kraken2_confidence.description: How much of a read has to agree before Kraken2 calls it at a taxon (Kraken2's --confidence).
kraken2_confidence.help_text: The fraction of a read's k-mers that must fall in a taxon or below it for the read to be called there; otherwise the call moves up the tree, or the read stays unclassified. 0.05 suits reads basecalled with a hac or sup model. Reads from a fast model have too many errors to reach it and come back almost all unclassified: use 0 for those.

kraken2_min_hit_groups.description: Independent database hits a read needs before Kraken2 calls it at all (Kraken2's --minimum-hit-groups).
kraken2_min_hit_groups.help_text: Kraken2's own default is 2; 3 asks for one more, which cuts calls made on a few stray matches.

min_reads.description: Taxa with fewer reads than this get below_threshold = true.
min_reads.help_text: Counts the reads Kraken2 assigned directly to the taxon. Flag-only: the taxon is still in taxon_abundance.tsv, with below_threshold = true. 0 disables.

min_rel_abundance.description: Taxa holding a smaller fraction of their sample's reads than this get below_threshold = true.
min_rel_abundance.help_text: The depth-independent counterpart of min_reads, as a fraction of the sample's host-removed reads: 0.0001 marks anything under 0.01%. A taxon is marked if it fails either cutoff. 0 disables.

kraken2_build_fasta.description: Genome FASTA(s) to build the Kraken2 database from, instead of downloading kraken2_db.
kraken2_build_fasta.help_text: A path or glob; needs kraken2_build_taxonomy too. For the test profile's synthetic genomes.

kraken2_build_taxonomy.description: Taxonomy for kraken2_build_fasta: a directory with nodes.dmp, names.dmp and seqid2taxid.map.
kraken2_build_taxonomy.help_text: nodes.dmp and names.dmp in NCBI's dump format; seqid2taxid.map gives each FASTA sequence ID's taxid, tab-separated.

amr_detection.title: AMR gene detection
amr_detection.description: Each host-removed read is searched for antimicrobial resistance genes.

amr_db.description: AMR gene database, from those bundled with ABRicate 1.4.0.
amr_db.help_text: ncbi (the default) is NCBI's Reference Gene Catalog, the genes AMRFinderPlus looks for. resfinder and argannot list acquired resistance genes. card and megares are advanced options: they also list housekeeping efflux pumps and their regulators (e.g. acrB, TolC, H-NS) that every cell of some species carries, so their results aren't comparable with the other three. Gene families and drug classes are NCBI's wherever a gene's sequence is also in the NCBI catalog, whichever database is picked.

amr_tool.description: How reads are matched to AMR genes.
amr_tool.help_text: minimap2 (the default) aligns reads to the genes in seconds. abricate runs ABRicate (BLAST) over the reads instead: it made the same calls in testing but takes about 25 times longer, roughly 45 minutes per 10 Gb flow cell.

amr_min_identity.description: Minimum percent identity for a read's match to a gene to count.
amr_min_identity.help_text: Nanopore reads have a few errors per hundred bases, so a read of a gene identical to the database's still matches it at a little under 100%. 90% allows for that while keeping apart gene families that differ by more.

amr_min_coverage.description: Minimum percent of a gene's length a read has to cover.
amr_min_coverage.help_text: A read that covers only part of a gene, for example at the end of the read, can't show the whole gene is there.

amr_intrinsic.description: Table of genes usually intrinsic to a genus (gene, genus, note).
amr_intrinsic.help_text: Fills amr_genes.tsv's intrinsic column. Defaults to assets/amr/intrinsic_genes.tsv; the test profile uses its own.

container_images.title: Container images
container_images.description: Where each tool's container image is pulled from.

container_registry.description: Registry for the biocontainers images (chopper, deacon, kraken2, minimap2, abricate, pandas).
container_registry.help_text: The google_batch profile points this at the project's own Artifact Registry mirror (see scripts/mirror_images.sh) so Batch VMs don't pull from quay.io; pass --container_registry quay.io to pull from upstream instead. The mirror keeps each image's upstream path, so only the host changes.

dockerhub_registry.description: Registry for the Docker Hub images (ubuntu, for database downloads and on Batch).
dockerhub_registry.help_text: Same idea as container_registry, for images that come from Docker Hub.

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options, typically left at their defaults.

help.description: Display the help message and exit.

tracedir.description: Directory for the Nextflow timeline/report/trace files.
